clue.text: Makes supplications audibly in worship

indicators.note: audibly tells us the word is heard spoken, and the spelling entered is a different one

parts.note: someone who makes supplications prays

explanation.surface: A worshipper praying out loud during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship a deity is to glorify and extol it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Exercise to have concert starting on time

indicators.note: starting puts the concert at the front of the exercise

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A fitness session must begin promptly with a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means punctual, arriving at exactly the scheduled moment.

clue.text: Provision of excellent neckwear worn by soldiers

indicators.note: worn by puts the soldiers inside the excellent letters, as if wearing them

parts.note: A1 is first class, excellent, written AI
men are soldiers in the ranks
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Smart neckties are issued to soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the letter I for the figure 1; 'worn by' puts the soldiers inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities provided, so a provision of comforts.

clue.text: Water group drying up

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A group of people discussing water drying up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sear is to scorch or wither, parching something dry.

clue.text: Food to consume — bravo! — in shopping centre?

indicators.note: in places the eating and the bravo inside the shopping centre

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
to consume food is to eat it
Bravo is the NATO alphabet code word for B

explanation.surface: Someone cheers at the prospect of a meal in a mall food court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo!' looks like applause but is the NATO code word for its letter; 'in' places the eating and that letter inside the shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a ball of minced meat, an example of a dish to eat.

clue.text: Fans the flames of old lover with super breast naughtily shown

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ace means super, excellent

indicators.note: naughtily suggests misbehaving letters, so breast is rearranged

explanation.surface: A former partner stokes jealousy by flashing a cleavage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges BREAST into RBATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan the flames is an idiom for making a bad situation worse.

clue.text: One vehicle and another overturning on pile of rocks

indicators.note: on in a down clue sets the first part above the second
overturning in a down clue turns the other vehicle upside down

parts.note: another vehicle, here a cart
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A vehicle crashes and flips over onto a rocky outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' turns CART into TRAC, sitting on TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a farm vehicle, an example of a machine for transport.

clue.text: A UK citizen in a place with many races

parts.note: a Scot is a UK citizen from Scotland

explanation.surface: A British person lives in a cosmopolitan place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many races' suggests ethnic diversity; ASCOT is an English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire hosting many horse meetings.

clue.text: Ill feeling of Heather keeping promise

indicators.note: keeping means the heather holds the promise inside it

parts.note: ling is a common type of heather
an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Heather harbours resentment despite a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike, a strong form of hostility.

clue.text: Like special road system? Nothing unexpected before a journey's end

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
something new is novel and unforeseen, so unexpected

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of the word journey's

explanation.surface: A motorist finds a trip ends without surprises on a special road layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' seems an anagram signal but simply gives NEW; 'end' takes the last letter of 'journey's', Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic system where vehicles may travel in only a single direction is described this way.

clue.text: The French fellow and companion going to a Spanish location

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a fellow is a man
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and his friend set off on a trip to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is short for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: La Mancha is a region of central Spain, famous as Don Quixote's home.

clue.text: What's nasty in goody-goody, first to expect entitlement

indicators.note: in puts the nasty word inside the word for a goody-goody

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous goody-goody
something nasty is vile

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of the word expect

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is unpleasant about a prim person who expects special treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage, so an entitlement.

clue.text: Head's sinking after new cinema releases

indicators.note: sinking after in a down clue puts the heads below the rearranged cinema
new suggests the letters of cinema made afresh in another order

parts.note: pate is an old word for head, so head's gives pates

explanation.surface: A manager's heart sinks after a new cinema opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CINEMA into EMANCI; 'Head's' becomes PATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set free, so it means releases.

clue.text: One very small bird by church

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A tiny bird perches beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is informal British slang for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is a nickname for a tiny person, someone notably little.

clue.text: Bring manager round for screening of film finally — film director too

indicators.note: bringing something round turns it about, so these letters are rearranged
finally picks out the last letter of the word film

explanation.surface: A film director is asked to bring his manager along to a screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges the first two words plus the last letter of the first 'film'; the second 'film' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingmar Bergman was the celebrated Swedish director of The Seventh Seal.

clue.text: One hermit seen wandering in county no longer

indicators.note: wandering suggests letters straying from their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone hermit is spotted roaming in a rural county.
explanation.walkthrough: MERIONETH was a Welsh county, abolished in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Merioneth is a former Welsh shire, now part of Gwynedd.

clue.text: Harbour stops giving signals

parts.note: a port is a harbour
ends are stops, as in comes to a stop

explanation.surface: A harbour halts traffic by giving signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or be an omen of, so it means signals.

clue.text: Bird making carrycot sheet messy

indicators.note: a messy sheet is crumpled and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A baby's carrycot sheet has been left in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' rearranges the letters of CARRYCOT SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading bird of the shore, a specific kind of avian.

clue.text: Plant in the middle of Kent facing direction of sunrise

indicators.note: in puts the plant inside the central letters
the middle of takes the central two letters of the word Kent

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A garden plant in the heart of Kent faces the sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kent' looks like the English county as a place, but only its two central letters are used, with 'in' wrapping them round the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in the east, so oriented that way means eastern.

clue.text: Spooner's manner, superior and crazy

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a way is a manner
higher means superior

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's ways were lofty and odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of WAY HIGHER and you hear HAY WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone haywire means out of control, erratic, so mad.

clue.text: Remained solemn in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as heard in speech, so we hear the word not see it

parts.note: staid means sober and solemn

explanation.surface: Someone stays serious while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means stopped on, continued in a place, a synonym of remained.

clue.text: Assignments with questions provided by teacher initially

indicators.note: provided by places the questions after the letter that supplies them
initially picks the opening letter of the word teacher

parts.note: to question is to ask, so questions is asks

explanation.surface: A teacher hands out homework accompanied by questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work set for someone, like assignments.

clue.text: Stand out, showing a measure of pushiness

indicators.note: a measure of means only a portion of the word pushiness is taken

explanation.surface: Someone excels by being a bit pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a measure of' takes SHINE from inside 'pushiness'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine is to excel, to be conspicuous among others.

clue.text: Be non-committal in a catty sort of way?

definitions.text: Be non-committal in a catty sort of way?

parts.words: Be non-committal in a catty sort of way?
parts.note: a cat's paw treads softly and cautiously; the verb for hedging is built from a word for a cat and a paw

explanation.surface: Someone avoids taking a stand, behaving like a wary cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty' suggests spite, but here it means cat-like, as in a cat's soft paw.
explanation.definitionFit: To act cautiously and evasively, avoiding commitment, is to tread warily like a cat.

clue.text: The top dog, not the last to get something to eat

parts.note: the top is number one, written NO plus I

indicators.note: not the last tells us the dog loses its final letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: The leading dog, not the one trailing behind, gets fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' looks like one phrase but splits: 'The top' is NO I (number one) and 'dog' is SETTER, which loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of meat, or a hazelnut chocolate, a food.

clue.text: Special attire making one irritable

definitions.meaning: a uniform worn by servants or members of a guild
an old sense meaning liverish, bad-tempered as from a disordered liver

explanation.surface: Wearing a uniform puts someone in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is a servant's uniform; livery also means liverish, cranky or tetchy.

clue.text: Most stony streets in which flier will settle

indicators.note: in which puts the flier between the two street abbreviations
will settle means the bird lands and rests inside the streets

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, so streets gives two of them
an erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Bleak, stony streets where a bird comes down to perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' and 'will settle' together put the sea eagle between the two street abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony in the sense of hard and unyielding; the superlative is the most severe.

clue.text: This writer coming to outdoor loo? It's engaged!

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a shed in the garden, jokingly an outdoor privy

explanation.surface: Someone heading to an outside toilet finds it occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' plays on a toilet's occupied sign, but means gears in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth that are interlocked are said to be engaged.
